content: Chloramphenicol reduces the effectiveness of cefuroxime through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents, such as chloramphenicol, may inhibit the activity of bactericidal agents like cefuroxime. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but caution is advised. Cefuroxime should not be co-administered with the cholera vaccine, as systemic antibiotics can act against the vaccine strain, reducing its efficacy. Patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination should not receive the cholera vaccine. Cefuroxime may increase the levels or effects of choline magnesium trisalicylate due to competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Cimetidine can decrease the levels or effects of cefuroxime by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin reduces the effectiveness of cefuroxime through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents like clarithromycin may inhibit the activity of bactericidal agents such as cefuroxime. Close monitoring is advised. Cefuroxime may reduce the effectiveness of cosibelimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Co-administration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. Demeclocycline decreases the effectiveness of cefuroxime via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents like demeclocycline may inhibit the activity of bactericidal agents such as cefuroxime. Close monitoring is recommended. Didanosine can reduce the levels or effects of cefuroxime by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Didanosine chewable tablets and oral solutions should be administered at least 2 hours before or several hours after cefuroxime. Monitor closely. Cefuroxime may reduce the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. While the risk of contraceptive failure is low, an alternative or additional form of birth control may be advisable during concurrent use. Monitor closely.
